title: Python — functions and collections
text: A Python function groups reusable steps and is defined with def. Parameters receive inputs; return sends a value to the caller. A function with no explicit return produces None. Lists are mutable ordered collections. Tuples are immutable sequences. Dictionaries map unique hashable keys to values. Sets hold distinct elements. Assignment such as b = a binds another name to the same object; it does not copy a list. Default argument values are evaluated when a function is defined. A mutable list default may therefore retain changes between calls. Use None as the default and create a new list inside the function when separate state is intended.

title: Python — iteration
text: A for loop visits items from an iterable. range(n) yields integers from zero through n minus one. A while loop repeats while its condition is true, so its body should eventually change the condition or exit explicitly. break exits the nearest enclosing loop; continue moves to its next iteration. A list comprehension constructs a list from an iterable, optionally with a filter. For example, [x*x for x in range(4)] gives [0, 1, 4, 9]. One loop that processes n values with constant work per value takes O(n) time. Two nested loops that each traverse n values take O(n squared) time when every pair is visited.

title: Databases — joining tables
text: An INNER JOIN returns row combinations satisfying the join predicate. A LEFT JOIN preserves every left row and supplies NULL for columns of an unmatched right row. The ON clause specifies the match condition. A CROSS JOIN forms a Cartesian product: three rows crossed with four rows produce twelve rows. Multiple matches on the right can produce more result rows than exist on the left. To find left rows without a match, use LEFT JOIN and test a non-nullable right key with IS NULL. A WHERE condition requiring a right-side value can remove unmatched rows from a left join. SQL tests missing values with IS NULL rather than = NULL.

title: Databases — normalization
text: Normalization organizes relations to reduce redundant facts and insertion, update, and deletion anomalies. A functional dependency X determines Y means that rows with equal X values must have equal Y values. First normal form requires atomic values within the chosen domain and no repeating groups. Second normal form additionally removes partial dependencies of non-key attributes on a proper subset of a candidate key. Third normal form restricts problematic transitive dependencies. If StudentID determines DepartmentID and DepartmentID determines DepartmentName, keeping department facts in a separate relation avoids repeating the department name for each student. In BCNF every determinant of a nontrivial functional dependency is a superkey. A lossless decomposition reconstructs the original relation when joined, without spurious rows.

title: Aptitude — ratios and percentages
text: A ratio compares quantities in the same units. To divide a total T in the ratio a:b, allocate T*a/(a+b) and T*b/(a+b). For example, dividing 100 in the ratio 2:3 gives 40 and 60. A percentage represents parts per hundred. Percentage change is (new minus old)/old times 100 when the old value is nonzero. Increasing 200 by 10 percent gives 220. Decreasing 220 by 10 percent gives 198, so equal percentage increases and decreases do not cancel. A weighted average divides the sum of each value times its weight by the total weight. Always identify the base quantity before calculating a percentage.

title: Aptitude — speed and time
text: For constant speed, distance equals speed times time. Use consistent units: one kilometer per hour equals five eighteenths meters per second. Average speed equals total distance divided by total elapsed time. For equal distances traveled at positive speeds a and b, average speed is 2ab/(a+b), not their arithmetic mean. For two objects moving toward each other, their relative speed is the sum of the speeds. When moving in the same direction, relative speed is their speed difference. A train passing a stationary point travels its own length; passing a platform requires traveling the train length plus the platform length.

title: English — reading comprehension
text: Reading comprehension distinguishes the main claim, supporting details, and inferences. The main idea expresses the passage's central point; an example usually supports that point rather than replacing it. An inference must follow from the available passage, not an unrelated assumption. Words such as however signal contrast, while therefore signals a conclusion. Resolve pronouns by checking the nearest contextually appropriate antecedent. To answer a vocabulary-in-context question, substitute the proposed meaning into the sentence and check the surrounding argument. When two options seem plausible, prefer the one whose full wording is supported; absolute claims such as always or never need correspondingly strong evidence.

title: Java — objects and inheritance
text: A Java class defines fields and methods; an object is an instance of a class. A constructor initializes a new instance and has no return type. Encapsulation controls access to state through access modifiers and methods. Inheritance lets a subclass extend a superclass. Overriding provides a subclass implementation of an inherited instance method with a compatible signature. Overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists. Dynamic dispatch selects an overridden instance method according to the runtime object type. An interface defines a contract that implementing classes satisfy. Prefer composition when one object uses another without a valid is-a relationship.

title: Machine learning — evaluation
text: Separate training data from evaluation data to estimate generalization. A validation set supports model selection; a held-out test set measures the final choice. Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at prediction time enters training or evaluation. Fit preprocessing such as scaling on training data only. For binary classification, precision is true positives divided by predicted positives, while recall is true positives divided by actual positives. Accuracy is the fraction of all predictions that are correct and can be misleading with strongly imbalanced classes. Overfitting occurs when a model captures training-specific noise and performs poorly on unseen data. Cross-validation repeats training and validation across multiple splits.
